rv.q: Both bleak and deeply human, this is a play whose intellectual intent never edges out its emotional capacity.

The stage version is realised with crystalline focus by Carrie Cracknell and acted with deep, pressing conviction by a central quartet of fine actors. It’s a tough watch – no one expects sunshine and happy endings with this subject matter – but that’s not the reason I kind of hated it.
The stark, unflinching treatment of this subject matter is well realised on Anna Yates's set, and it does not sugarcoat the emotionally messy nature of the process.
And it really does shine on the Donmar's small stage, where an audience can see close-up how a single space shifts from an impersonal meeting place into an almost spiritual site of reconciliation.
Cracknell's production is exquisitely focused, finely wrought: the performances vibrate.
The great strength of Mass — its grown-up understanding that there are no easy answers — is also its limitation as a piece of drama.
Certainly, little is gained in the transition to the stage.
Up close with grief in a starkly haunting play
That's the best play I'll see this year.
Under Carrie Cracknell's empathic direction... this is undoubtedly another triumph for the Donmar.

Cracknell, fresh from her triumph with Arcadia at the Old Vic, marshals all of this with economy and precision, deftly introducing some unexpected catharsis and a glimpse of value, in this bleak encounter, for the young lad watching from the wings.

When the play leans into its essence of four people grappling with something unspeakable, it becomes deeply moving, even suffocating in its intimacy. Yet for all its emotional precision, Mass struggles with pacing, particularly in moments where repetition begins to dull rather than deepen the impact.
At its best, Mass is a mesmerising fusion of incisive writing and extraordinary performances.
It’s a masterful piece of writing from Kranz: every utterance counts, and each line is a turn of a cog that keeps this grim yet poignant narrative moving.
There is little dramatic tension and a drift into the sentimental

cn.t: Critics praise this intense, claustrophobic drama about parents meeting after a school shooting as devastatingly powerful and beautifully performed, though some find its naturalistic approach overly gruelling and emotionally manipulative.
